newsitem.title: USA: US House Democrats to introduce brownfields bill.
newsitem.headline: US House Democrats to introduce brownfields bill.

text.p: U.S. House Democrats plan to introduce a bill Wednesday to spur the redevelopment of abandoned, polluted industrial sites across the country.
Details of the brownfields bill were not immediately available, but House aides said Tuesday it was similar to legislation offered in the last Congress.

In a bipartisan bill introduced in 1995, House lawmakers proposed to provide $15 million a year in grants to local governments to assess contamination at brownfield sites, lend money for cleanups, and protect new purchasers and redevelopers from liabilities for past pollution.

While Democrats and Republicans both want to encourage brownfields renewal to help revive the economies of cities and communities nationwide, Republicans have linked the issue to an overhaul of the Superfund toxic waste cleanup program.
The two parties have been deadlocked for the last three years over how to improve the Superfund law, so the Democrats are trying to pass a brownfields bill on its own.
"The search for comprehensive reform shouldn't stand in the way of legislation on a consensus basis ... where there's already broad agreement," said an aide to House Commerce Committee Democrats.
The bill has no Republican sponsors yet, but Democrat aides said that they were going to work next to find Republican sponsors.
